page: Amazon Web Services m5ad.24xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture, featuring 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 7571 processor running at 2.2 GHz. The instance supplies 384 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware accelerators such as discrete GPUs are not bundled in this configuration.

Storage capabilities include 3,600 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD instance storage, providing low-latency temporary block storage directly attached to the host server. Network throughput is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 20 Gbps. Cryptographic extensions such as AES and SHA-NI are active, alongside AVX, BMI2, and FMA instruction sets, though modern vector extensions such as AVX-512 are not present on this CPU generation.

Benchmark evaluations indicate distinct characteristics between single-threaded and multi-threaded throughput. Single-core performance occupies the bottom tier across metrics, reflecting the 2.2 GHz base frequency with a stress-ng single-core score of 590.99 and a Geekbench single-core result of 725.0. Conversely, parallel execution leverages the 96 compute threads to deliver mid-tier results, such as a PassMark CPU score of 47,316.06 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression of 38.57 GB/sec. Hardware-assisted cryptography performs well, achieving a PassMark CPU encryption score of 77,626.79, while small-block cached memory bandwidth reaches 3,712.61 GB/sec.

The dense core count combined with substantial memory and integrated high-capacity NVMe storage makes the m5ad.24xlarge cost-efficient for parallel data-processing tasks that benefit from fast scratch storage. The profile is appropriate for multi-threaded batch workloads, distributed caching tiers like Redis, static web serving pools, and enterprise database hosting requiring local non-volatile cache.
description: Amazon Web Services m5ad.24xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro instance providing 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores using AMD EPYC 7571 processors clocked at 2.2 GHz. It is equipped with 384 GB of DDR4 memory, 3,600 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local storage, and a baseline network speed of 20 Gbps, without dedicated GPUs. Benchmark assessments reveal lower-tier single-core compute performance, as reflected in Geekbench and compression metrics, balanced by mid-range multi-core scaling and strong hardware cryptographic throughput. The high thread count and large NVMe disk array provide practical resource density for multi-threaded batch operations, database hosting with high-speed temporary storage requirements, distributed caching, and static web serving.
